intent: Trace the change in world population from 1800 to 2014 using the provided data.

requirements.question: How does the video present the required area marks in this chart?
Trace the change in world population from 1800 to 2014.

units.claim: All 1 required area marks are present in the chart: world population.
accept: every listed area, reference mark, segment, or category is visible
each mark is correctly bound to its entity or series identity
reject: missing any required area, reference mark, segment, or category
assigning a mark to the wrong entity, panel, or series
replacing a required mark with narration text alone

units.claim: World population increased from 1.02 billion in 1800 to 8.00 billion in 2014.
accept: World population rose from about 1.02 billion to 8.00 billion between 1800 and 2014.
The world population increased by approximately 6.98 billion over the period.
reject: World population was 8.00 billion in 1800 and 1.02 billion in 2014.

optional_valid: The area chart shows a generally upward trend over the period.
unsupported_to_avoid: World population growth was constant or linear.
World population exceeded any specific threshold not present in the data.
World population will continue to grow after 2014.
The chart shows multiple countries or regions.
review_notes: Only one analytical slot is required because the intent asks for the overall change from start to end.
The change unit uses the first and last rows as endpoints; intermediate rows support the trend but are not separately required.
